title: Urgency pressure
evidence: The message pushes the reader to act within a short deadline.
explanation: Scammers create time pressure so people act before verifying.

title: Generic greeting
evidence: The message opens with a non-specific greeting.
explanation: Legitimate organisations usually address you by name.

title: Authority impersonation
evidence: The message claims to come from a bank, a government body, or an official agency.
explanation: Impersonating an authority makes the request feel official.

title: Credential or KYC request
evidence: The message asks for credentials, identity details, or a KYC update.
explanation: No legitimate organisation asks for OTPs, PINs, passwords, or full identity data by message.

title: Unusual payment request
evidence: The message asks for payment through an unusual or untraceable method.
explanation: Untraceable payment demands such as gift cards or crypto are a common fraud pattern.

title: Prize or reward bait
evidence: The message claims the reader has won a prize, lottery, refund, or reward.
explanation: Unexpected winnings are used to bait people into paying a fee or sharing details.

title: Case or FIR claim
evidence: The message claims a case, FIR, or legal action has been filed against the reader.
explanation: Real agencies do not demand payment over a message or call.

title: Secrecy demand
evidence: The message tells the reader not to discuss it with anyone.
explanation: Isolation prevents victims from getting a second opinion.

title: Pressure to stay on the line
evidence: The message insists the reader stay on a call or chat without disconnecting.
explanation: Keeping the victim engaged blocks independent verification.

title: Verification-fee demand
evidence: The message demands a fee to 'verify', 'clear', or 'settle' the reader's case.
explanation: Any demand to pay to avoid arrest or clear your name is a scam.

title: App installation lure
evidence: The message asks the reader to install an app, share the screen, or download a file.
explanation: Fake apps and remote-access tools give scammers control of the device.
